newsitem.title: USA: U.S. fighter crashes off Florida.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fighter crashes off Florida.

text.p: A U.S. Air Force F-16 jet fighter crashed into Florida Bay south of Miami on Tuesday, possibly after hitting another F-16 flying nearby, defence officials said.
The pilot of the crashed jet, from Homestead Air Reserve Base, ejected safely at about 11:45 a.m. EST and was picked up uninjured by a U.S. Coast Guard helicopter about 20 minutes later.
The second fighter returned safely to the base. "It had a slight amount of damage to it, very, very slight," Major Bobby D'Angelo, the base spokesman, said.
Neither pilot's name was immediately available.
A defence official in Washington who asked not to be identified said the two aircraft crashed into one another. D'Angelo said he could not confirm that had happened.
"It's possible that they could have touched each other. They didn't actually smash into each other," he said. "We're investigating it."
A Coast Guard spokesman said the pilot of the jet that crashed had been taken to the hospital at the U.S. Navy's Air Station Boca Chica in the Florida Keys. "He is fine," he said.
